name: RICE
summary: A pioneering in-ice radio experiment at the South Pole used Antarctic ice to search for ultra-high-energy neutrino showers and establish techniques later adopted by ARA.
physics_targets: Radio attenuation, reflection and propagation in polar ice
detection_principle: Buried dipole antennas measured impulsive radio Cherenkov emission from the net charge in a neutrino-induced shower. Coincident waveforms and reconstructed vertices were used to suppress noise.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final major exposure is explicitly 1999–2010; ARA is identified as the succeeding initiative.

timeline.event: Early antennas deployed in association with AMANDA boreholes.

collaboration.name: RICE Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Original sensor array
key_parameters.value: 20 dipole antennas in a three-dimensional in-ice grid

results.summary: No convincing neutrino candidates were found in the twelve-year exposure; 95% confidence flux limits and ice-property studies were published.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
